clue.text: Might an unwanted president's life be said to have started here?

definitions.text: Might an unwanted president's life be said to have started here?

blocks.note: a gooseberry is the unwanted third person tagging along with a couple
the surname of two US presidents

explanation.surface: A wry wonder about where an unpopular president's life began.
explanation.walkthrough: Children were traditionally told that babies were found under a gooseberry bush, so the whole clue is the definition while its words also build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery folklore tells children that newborn babies are discovered under this garden shrub.

clue.text: Does life here expose one's id?

definitions.text: Does life here expose one's id?

blocks.clueFragment: Does life here expose one's id?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about psychoanalysis laying bare the unconscious self
setter's reading: a place where living is fully visible to onlookers, so nothing private stays hidden

explanation.surface: A psychologist's question about whether some way of living lays bare the inner self.
explanation.walkthrough: The id sounds like Freud, but the clue means a situation of total public scrutiny, like a pet fish seen from every side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a situation without privacy, where every action is watched by observers.

clue.text: Basket maker that's old raised cash in Brazil once

indicators.note: in a down clue, something raised is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: common abbreviation for old
reis were the former currency units of Brazil and Portugal

explanation.surface: A basket weaver described as elderly who once made money in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: This willow's flexible twigs are the material traditionally woven into baskets and wickerwork.

clue.text: Reel in crew a bit

blocks.note: a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
some means a certain amount, a bit

explanation.surface: Someone staggering slightly among a boat's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Reel looks like a verb about staggering, but it is the Scottish dance; an eightsome reel is danced by eight people.
explanation.definitionFit: The eightsome is a lively Scottish country dance performed by eight dancers together.

clue.text: Overshadow desirable time by drabness afterwards?

blocks.note: to eclipse is to overshadow
a plum job is a desirable one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something pleasant is followed by a dull period that casts it into shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Male ducks moult after breeding into a dull, female-like dress; the question mark flags this ornithological sense of drabness.
explanation.definitionFit: Male ducks wear this dull moult coat after the breeding season ends, losing their bright colours.

clue.text: Prize-winning appeal, it's told, is self-explanatory

blocks.note: first meaning: at a fairground strength machine, sounding the chime at the top wins the prize, so it means scoring a success
second meaning: a summons by a church or door chime, which announces its own purpose to all who hear it

explanation.surface: Praise for some award-winning attraction so obvious it needs no comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means scoring a success, from the fairground test of strength; it is also literally a call to come, which needs no explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means achieving success, from winning at the fairground strength machine, and literally a summons by chime.

clue.text: Support oneself with twine

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
the id is the self in Freudian psychology

explanation.surface: Holding oneself up with the help of some string.
explanation.definitionFit: To braid is to interweave strands, the same action as to twine them together.

clue.text: Steel trap sprung by one with part in old plot

definitions.text: one with part in old plot

indicators.note: a sprung trap has snapped open, so its pieces end up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A trap set off by a conspirator in some old scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The old plot is the Gunpowder Plot of 1605; potassium nitrate is a main ingredient of gunpowder, so it played its part.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate is a key ingredient of gunpowder, central to Guy Fawkes's 1605 conspiracy against Parliament.

clue.text: Prone to romance

blocks.note: first meaning: stretched out flat
second meaning: inventing fanciful stories, telling untruths

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to fall in love easily.
explanation.walkthrough: Prone to romance reads as a phrase about amorous people; split it into two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lying flat, and also telling falsehoods, which is what romancing means as an activity.

clue.text: Note to brother in blood

blocks.note: drop someone a line means send a short note
a brother in arms is an ally

explanation.surface: A letter written to a sibling by blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Descending in a direct family line, by blood inheritance from parent to child.

clue.text: What's left of life in song?

definitions.text: What's left of life in song?

blocks.clueFragment: What's left of life in song?
blocks.note: surface reading: whatever remains of a life once it is told in music
setter's reading: the song says life is just a bowl of fruit, and the clue asks what remains once the bowl is eaten

explanation.surface: A melancholy question about what remains of a life after it is sung about.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is 'Life Is Just a Bowl of Cherries'; once the fruit is eaten, only the pits are left.
explanation.definitionFit: Pits are the hard leftovers after eating the fruit that the popular song compares life to.

clue.text: Main platform for performing poet

indicators.note: a performer puts on an act, so these letters are put through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: The principal stage set aside for a poet giving a reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is the old word for the open sea, so a main platform is one on a ship, at the head of the foremast.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship it is the platform at the top of the foremast, a structure at sea.

clue.text: From top to bottom?

blocks.note: surface reading: a direction, from the summit down to the base
setter's reading: covering everything thoroughly, the full vertical extent of a subject

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a direction of travel, but it means thorough, measured from the surface down to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough, comprehensive treatment covers a subject completely, as if measured all the way down.

clue.text: Mural is not long and firm

blocks.note: a sec, short for second, is no time at all
abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A wall painting described as short in length and solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Secco is a wall painting done on dry plaster, as opposed to fresco on wet plaster.

clue.text: Time to give new heart to Spanish region's torpidity

indicators.note: a new heart means the central letter of the region is swapped out for another

blocks.note: the north-eastern Spanish region centred on Barcelona
abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A call for a sluggish Spanish region to be revitalised.
explanation.walkthrough: CATALONIA has nine letters, so its heart is the fifth, L, which T replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a state of stupor and immobility, an extreme form of torpor or sluggishness.

clue.text: This may stiffen chopper

blocks.note: first meaning: a kitchen whisk that beats whites until stiff
second meaning: slang for a helicopter, from its whirling rotors

explanation.walkthrough: Chopper looks like an axe or knife; here it is a helicopter, slangily called by the same name as the kitchen whisk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary whisk stiffens egg whites, and the same name is slang for a helicopter.

clue.text: Language that's generated for hurling at openers

indicators.note: hurling things sends them flying, so these letters land in a different order

blocks.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Abusive language generated to throw at a cricket side's opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Generated marks a language built deliberately rather than evolved; openers suggests cricket's first two batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the best-known constructed international tongue, invented by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Spooner's sports equipment could be a little spread

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: a putter is a golf club and a bat is for cricket

explanation.surface: A note that some sporting gear could be something to put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A small moulded portion of butter is a little amount of something spread on toast.

clue.text: See 4
See 5
Devotion for drug bringing about shame

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: it's a shame means it's a pity
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tale of a narcotic causing disgrace instead of religious devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devoutness, reverence and dutiful devotion to God.

clue.text: Artist showing power of current with his water

blocks.note: the watt is the unit of electrical power
the French word for water, his because the painter was French

explanation.surface: A painter of rivers depicting their flow and force.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter was French, so his water is the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was an eighteenth-century French painter of fêtes galantes.

clue.text: One's not allowed in Ely, it might be said

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: Ely was once the Isle of Ely, so someone barred from it is from a former isle

explanation.surface: Someone barred from entering the cathedral city of Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, stood on the Isle of Ely amid the fens; someone banished is put out of the isle.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished and forbidden to enter their homeland.

clue.text: Subject of gossip, as far as one can tell

definitions.text: as far as one can tell

blocks.note: first meaning: someone talked about is said to have ears burning

blocks.clueFragment: as far as one can tell
blocks.note: second meaning: the range within which a voice can be heard, so within telling distance

explanation.surface: A hedge on the reliability of some gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Burning ears are said to signal you are being discussed, so the gossiped-about person has ears hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which sound can be heard, so how far a message may be told.

clue.text: Linger by resort's river

blocks.note: Hove is a seaside resort next to Brighton
abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Lingering beside a river at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside resort on England's south coast, twinned with Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to remain hanging about in one place, waiting or lingering nearby.

clue.text: Secret hint

blocks.note: first meaning, an adjective: private, personal
second meaning, a verb: suggest indirectly

explanation.surface: A tip passed on confidentially.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate as an adjective means private and personal; as a verb it means suggest or imply.

clue.text: Actor getting three points out of four

indicators.note: out of here means on the outside of, so some letters sit around another

blocks.note: north, east and north again, compass points
Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A performer scoring three marks out of a possible four.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of four reads as a score, but out of means outside: the points go around the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: David Niven was a British film star, famous for The Guns of Navarone.

clue.text: Disarming quote spreads around: "Have wealth - do split"

blocks.note: to fare well is to prosper
a to-do split in two leaves its first part
arms are what spread around someone in an embrace

explanation.surface: A disarming saying about wealth being shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose and our reading is a best guess: prosper, half of a to-do, and limbs that spread around. The title is Hemingway's novel, taken from George Peele's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying goodbye to weapons is literally laying them down, and the title is a quotation from Peele.
